svg.text: section B-B through the plate, section C-C through a spring

1. TrapStops — ledges welded to the front and both side walls. They stop the plate flush and are the whole trick: the trap can rotate down but never up, so a hook or a hand pulling a parcel back out only jams it shut harder.
2. Cranked hinge: the pin sits 12 mm below the plate and its knuckles interleave with the fixed leaves, so the plate cannot be levered off the pin from the throat.
3. TrapSprings — two torsion springs, coil Ø18, wire Ø3.2, 9¼ turns, one tail bearing under the plate. Anchor the reaction tail on a slotted bracket: set the preload so a 500 g parcel trips the trap.
4. Front stiffener lip, 20 deep, keeps the free edge straight so the plate cannot be bent past the side ledges.
5. TrapDoor — 3 mm plate, 318 x 394, set 170 below the rim. Swing shown at 62°; a deep parcel pushes it on round to vertical, giving the full 296 mm of throat.
